answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can run on rotating shared custody: every identity must periodically take custody of a communal work queue for a full epoch, verifying peers' submissions and keeping it moving, like a stallholder guarding the onyx counter one week and the ivory shelf the next. Custody is live and unpredictable, so one operator cannot staff many identities at once. Missing a duty or rubber-stamping bad work slashes the stake and a timber-grade reputation score that takes many honest epochs to rebuild. The price is attention, so cloning multiplies workload, not reward.
